title: Le Petit Voyage
tagline: Bonjour, la classe, la famille, et le marche du samedi
description: A gentle first trip in French. From a first bonjour on the square to the classroom, home, and a Saturday market story, every street and stall speaks simple French and the learner answers in it.
worldPrompt: An original, cozy French town adventure for A1 true beginners. The learner arrives in a small town with a sunny square, a bakery, a school, and a Saturday market. No real public figures appear: the baker, the teacher, the classmates, the grandparents at the market, and the market seller are all original. Each chapter gates one French unit: greetings and politeness with bonjour, bonsoir, salut, monsieur, madame, merci; asking and giving a name with je m appelle and comment tu t appelles; classroom objects and colors with un, une, and c est; family with mon, ma, mes and la mere, le pere, la soeur, le frere; home and the week with la maison, la cuisine, and lundi through dimanche; and a short A1 graded reader market story Une journee au marche with colors, family, and polite market language. Loot is small town things: bakery ticket, school badge, family photo, market basket, warm baguette. Tone warm, unhurried, and encouraging. French words appear with a quick English gloss when first seen, exactly as the course lessons do.

characters.name: you
characters.bio: The new arrival. You learn one French word at a time and use it before the next one comes.

characters.name: Mme Martin
characters.bio: Runs the market fruit stall. Polite and patient. She answers bonjour with bonjour and waits for s il vous plait before she wraps the apples.

characters.name: Luc
characters.bio: Your classmate. Knows salut for friends and bonjour monsieur for adults, and will whisper mon, ma, mes when you need it.

characters.name: Maitresse Dubois
characters.bio: The primary school teacher. Keeps un and une straight and says c est un stylo bleu slowly so every child can repeat it.

characters.name: Mamie et Papi
characters.bio: Grandparents at the market every Saturday. They answer bonjour with a smile and say merci beaucoup when you offer a pomme.

chapters.title: La Place du Bonjour
chapters.hook: The square says bonjour first. Answer it and learn when bonsoir and salut belong.
chapters.musicPrompt: Bright small town morning. Light accordion with gentle strings, warm and unhurried, instrumental only, no vocals.

chapters.title: La Classe de Couleurs
chapters.hook: A desk, a tray, a board: name them with un and une and add the color that follows.
chapters.musicPrompt: Quiet classroom air. Soft piano over warm woodwinds, calm and focused, instrumental only, no vocals.

chapters.title: La Maison et la Semaine
chapters.hook: Home has rooms, the week has days. Say where you live and what day it is.
chapters.musicPrompt: Homey afternoon light. Warm guitar and soft piano, cozy and unhurried, instrumental only, no vocals.

chapters.title: Le Marche du Samedi
chapters.hook: The stalls are set, the story is ready. Read Une journee au marche and buy politely with je voudrais.
chapters.musicPrompt: Market day finale. Cheerful bustle with light percussion and warm accordion, quietly triumphant when the baguette is shared, instrumental only, no vocals.

loot.name: Ticket de la Boulangerie
loot.description: The baker's queue ticket from the square. Chapter 1, the first bonjour.

loot.name: Badge de la Classe
loot.description: A small enamel badge that says un stylo bleu on one side and une trousse rouge on the other. Chapter 2, the classroom.

loot.name: Photo de Famille
loot.description: A wallet photo labeled mon pere, ma mere, ma soeur, mon frere. Chapter 3, the family table.

loot.name: Panier du Marche
loot.description: The wicker basket from Mme Martin's stall, smelling of pommes rouges. Chapter 4, the market story.

loot.name: Baguette Chaude
loot.description: The warm baguette everyone shares when the story ends. Given when you can greet, name, order, sort, and buy politely in French. Legendary town clear.
